phase3_findings.description: install.sh section 4b digests SOURCE bytes for setup-action, provision-helper, implement-workflow and manifest while recording consumer runtime paths, but install_managed PRESERVES a modified/unverified/unreadable artifact (sidecar .prflow-new) and the tier1_rc != 0 arm skips the workflow copy loop entirely. check_readiness then returns digest-mismatch and provision-lint-tools.sh _die's, hard-failing the whole cloud implement job permanently, with a printed remedy (re-run the installer) that cannot converge.

Same defect: the marker binds SOURCE digests for components install.sh may deliberately preserve or skip, so a supported install outcome hard-fails every later implement run with a non-remedy. The guard's comparand comes from a producer that does not emit it on every path the guard now selects.

Same defect, with the availability consequence traced: the _die is a hard exit 1 inside a step of `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-project-env` with no continue-on-error, so the entire /prflow:implement job fails. Three routine non-adversarial paths reach it (hand-edited workflow or action; pre-manifest installation upgrading, where every differing artifact classifies unverified; plugin auto-update replacing the vendored readers).

The new hardensetup step displaces PR-head bytes for .github/actions/setup-project-env/ but publishes no displaced_paths output and is absent from displaced_join's three-producer env, so HARDENED_PATHS omits it and the reviewing agent reads base-ref bytes from the working tree as if they were head — on exactly the file a PR editing that action would be under review for. That workflow states the governing contract inline for its other producers.

The readiness-refusal remedy string 'remedy: re-run the PRFlow installer (install.sh) so the marker matches the installed components' is false against HEAD for the dominant digest-mismatch cause (a preserved local edit): re-running reproduces the identical marker and preserves the edit again. Self-contradicting-diff carve-out.

The TOOLS comment states a consequence the code does not produce: TOOLS is a hardcoded literal, not a function of the manifest, and an out-of-manifest tool cannot ride a partial cache restore (rc-4 hard refusal / rc-3 degrade). A maintainer could 'fix' a hazard that does not exist by loosening the real refusal. Self-contradicting-diff carve-out.

TOOLS is a third independent copy of the tool set beside lint_manifest.KNOWN_TOOLS and lint_provision.KNOWN_TOOLS, with no mechanical link; a manifest declaring a tool this list omits would have that tool silently never provisioned while the readiness gate still said READY.

Vendored helper components are bound by install-time digest at $pin but resolved at run time from a ref install.sh may not control: devflow_pin_version keeps an existing deliberate pin, and install.sh falls back to PIN=$REF (possibly a mutable branch) in the curl-piped case. The 'identical bytes at the pinned ref' comment is false against HEAD.

build_state does not close the round trip its docstring promises: component names and recorded paths are copied through unchecked, so a marker that validate_state later rejects is published successfully and the failure surfaces at provisioning time on the consumer rather than at publication time. Confirmed by execution.

Plan.__init__(status, **kw) silently absorbs unknown keywords and requires tool/os/arch on no status, so a misspelled field is a silently None attribute and an under-populated established plan yields a cache_key containing the literal None — the exact stale-binary failure cache_key exists to prevent. Confirmed by execution.

The SCRIPTS_DIR fallback has no third arm verifying the chosen directory contains the helpers (it probes only lint_provision.py while the helper also invokes install_state.py), so a failed vendor materialization is misreported as a marker-readiness failure and sends the operator to the wrong remedy.

The hardening step drives a destructive rm -f selection through grep, a non-preflight PATH tool, on the left of ||, so set -e/pipefail cannot fire and a missing grep deletes every trusted file just materialized; the job aborts only incidentally via the next existence check, with a misattributed message. The fetch's stderr is also discarded on a security-critical fail-closed arm.

The compatibility tuple is transcribed twice — COMPONENTS in lib/generate-install-state.py and install.sh section 4b's --component operands — with nothing reconciling the copies, so a component added to one side silently narrows every consumer's marker while both the drift gate and the 4b end-to-end tests stay green. Corroborated by the Phase 3.1.5 completeness critic.

Completeness critic: the audit's COMPONENTS set is a superset of an independently derived enumeration (import graph + action/helper invocation graph + lint_mode-passing workflows), so it is complete with respect to that signal. But the population is enumerated twice with no reconciliation, so the --check drift gate certifies completeness only for the repo-local copy and is structurally blind to the consumer copy the feature ships.

A structural-pin-ok declaration covers a log message, not a contract: the pinned literal 'no lint-tool provisioning and no manifest validation' is the body of an echo in action.yml consumed by no tool, declared routing-dispatch-contract. Rewording it turns the suite RED with no behavior change. Per the repo review extension this is a wording-only pin and at least Important.

The composite action's lint-provisioning step body has zero executable coverage: the closed lint_mode case, the RUNNER_OS/RUNNER_ARCH mapping tables (an unreconciled mirror of lint_provision.KNOWN_OS/KNOWN_ARCH), and the SCRIPTS_DIR fallback are covered only by substring pins on file text.

The GITHUB_PATH export is never exercised — _run_helper_1388 pops GITHUB_PATH from the environment, so the append that makes the provisioned tools visible to the model runs in no test; deleting it leaves every fail-closed arm green while the model never sees shellcheck/ruff on PATH.
tar.xz — the archive type every real shellcheck artifact uses — is never extracted in a test; _mk_archive_1388 builds only tar.gz and the one non-gz case is zip.
The drift gate has no RED-direction test: the suite only asserts --check exits 0 on the current tree, so an inverted comparison would leave the gate inert and nothing would say so.

The multi-tool loop is never run: every fixture passes tools=shellcheck while production TOOLS defaults to 'shellcheck ruff', leaving PROVISIONED/UNPROVISIONED accumulation and the partial-failure ordering untested.

The section 4b positive control asserts structural validity (load_state status established), never readiness (check_readiness ready) against the consumer tree — which is exactly what would have caught the Critical marker-skew defect.

The unwritable-target fixture chmods a parent to 0o555 with no os.geteuid() != 0 guard, inconsistent with two sibling permission fixtures in the same file that do guard on root; under uid 0 it is an environment-dependent RED with no attribution.

Nothing verifies the pinned digests against upstream reality — every test computes its own fixture digest, so the wrong pin on main would have hard-failed provisioning on every real runner while the suite stayed green. A periodic network-permitted re-derivation job is the only check for this class.

generate-install-state.py raises untyped tracebacks where every sibling reader returns a typed reason (unguarded json.loads of .prflow/config.json), and main silently ignores unrecognized argv, so a typo like --chek writes the marker instead of checking it.

Section 4b's outer guard has no else arm, so a source tree missing the manifest or install_state.py installs no manifest and no marker, prints nothing, and exits 0 — the only silent arm in a block where every other refusal logs a warning naming its cause.

All four new types leave __delattr__ unguarded and expose their payload by reference, so `del r.state` yields established==True with state unreachable — the shape the constructor works hardest to make unrepresentable — and a certified payload can be mutated in place after certification.
StateResult('established', ...) checks only that state is not None, so it accepts a payload validate_state would refuse (e.g. an empty components object). Holds today by call-site discipline only.

cloud-setup.md's fail-closed list groups readiness reasons with per-tool ones and closes 'each naming the tool', but the readiness gate fires before any tool is selected and emits through _die - . Behavior-inert prose cap applied (both limbs hold: docs/internal is unread by tools and pruned from the vendor slice).

install.md tells consumers their marker is regenerated by lib/generate-install-state.py; that helper's own docstring scopes itself to the primary repo's committed copy and hardcodes _REPO_ROOT, so from a vendored copy it would resolve to the vendor tree. Behavior-inert prose cap applied.

install_state.py's docstring names COMPONENTS in lib/generate-install-state.py as the authoritative set, but the consumer publication path (install.sh section 4b) never consults it. The two agree today; the parenthetical presents one as authoritative for a path it does not govern. Behavior-inert prose cap applied.

The release note's 'can never execute a setup action edited in the pull request under review' is narrowly true of setup-project-env only; read-project-config and vendor-plugin remain PR-head-resolved in the same runner. VC-54 graded the scoped wording accurate, so this stays a clarity Suggestion rather than a promoted falsehood.

Added comment blocks exceed the prevention-only three-line cap and carry derivation rather than the wrong change they prevent: devflow-runner.yml:1393-1403 (11 lines), ci.yml:73-79 (7 lines), and provision-lint-tools.sh's cache/re-verification (6) and pre-provisioned-reuse (4) comments.

The new lint-manifest job was inserted between the jobs-level comment block describing the shard partition and the shard job it documents, so that comment now heads the wrong job and shard: is left undocumented. Capped at Suggestion in the report (organizational, behavior-inert workflow comment).

A missing unzip/tar on a Windows Git Bash or minimal self-hosted runner hard-fails the whole implement job, in tension with the CLAUDE.md convention this same PR adds (reserve fail-closed for integrity checks). AC10 lists 'missing installer primitive' among the fail-closed arms, so the two statements now disagree in-tree.

_die bypasses the RETURN trap (exit 1 does not run a RETURN trap), leaking the mktemp -d work directory on every fail-closed arm. Cosmetic on an ephemeral runner; the suite does drive the helper repeatedly in one process.

REFUTED — filed as Critical that the changed shellcheck linux/x86_64 digest was hand-edited (inferred from the 60-of-64 shared hex prefix between old and new). The orchestrator downloaded shellcheck-v0.10.0.linux.x86_64.tar.xz and ruff-0.6.9-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz from upstream and computed sha256: the NEW values are correct and the value on main was wrong. pr-test-analyzer and the final-pass reviewer independently downloaded and reached the same conclusion. This PR FIXES a bad supply-chain pin. Not filed as a finding.
